{{Short description|American mathematician (1948–2019)}}
'''Terrence Staples''' ('''Terry''') '''Millar''' (September 18, 1948 – March 9, 2019) was professor emeritus of mathematics and former associate dean for physical sciences in the Graduate School and assistant to the provost at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].  He joined the math faculty in 1976 after serving two years in the Marines and obtaining a Ph.D. from [[Cornell University]].<ref name="Obituary">{{cite news |title=Millar was math professor, noted UW–Madison research administrator |url=https://news.wisc.edu/millar-remembered-for-contributions-to-mathematical-logic-science-education/ |access-date=25 March 2021 |publisher=Wisconsin News |date=March 15, 2019}}</ref>  Millar retired in 2015 and was considered to be one of the world's foremost researchers in computable model theory.<ref name="Math">{{cite web |title=In Memoriam: Terry Millar |url=https://www.math.wisc.edu/node/758 |website=Department of Mathematics |publisher=University of Wisconsin Madison |access-date=25 March 2021}}</ref>

==Biography==
He earned a bachelor’s degree in mathematics from Cornell University in 1970 and his Ph.D. in Mathematics from Cornell University in 1975.<ref name="Madison">{{cite news |title=Millar, Terrence S. |url=https://madison.com/news/local/obituaries/millar-terrence-s/article_21289a74-afad-5e17-8e96-bbb2c3c4ab89.html |access-date=25 March 2021 |publisher=Madison.com |date=March 13, 2019}}</ref>

Millar died March 9, 2019, at the age of 70 due to pancreatic cancer.<ref name="Obituary" />

==Career==
Along with physics professors [[Sau Lan Wu]] and [[Wesley Smith (academic)]], he “was central to Wisconsin’s contribution to development of the Large Hadron Collider.”<ref name="Ron">{{cite news |last1=Seely |first1=Ron |title=UW has big role in giant particle collider |url=https://lacrossetribune.com/couleenews/news/local/uw-has-big-role-in-giant-particle-collider/article_9d66fd0a-e41e-57ac-9a8b-d0521eaacab6.html |access-date=25 March 2021 |publisher=La Crosse Tribune |date=September 10, 2008}}</ref><ref name="Higgs">{{cite news |last1=Sakai |first1=Jill |title=UW scientists play key role in discovery of a new particle consistent with Higgs boson |url=https://news.wisc.edu/uw-scientists-play-key-role-in-discovery-of-a-new-particle-consistent-with-higgs-boson/ |access-date=25 March 2021 |publisher=UWM News Reports |date=July 4, 2012}}</ref> Working alongside [[Francis Halzen]], he was “integral in launching the [[IceCube Neutrino Observatory|IceCube South Pole Neutrino Observatory]].”<ref name="Obituary" />
